title: The error norm of the automatic step size of CSolverExplicit scales by max(q_new, q_start) without absolute values
author: Claude-JG
description: CSolverExplicitTimeInt computes the scale of the error of ODE23 and DOPRI5 as absoluteTolerance + Maximum(q_second, q_start)*relativeTolerance for the coordinates, velocities and ODE1 coordinates, without the absolute values: a negative coordinate makes the scale smaller than the absolute tolerance, zero or negative, so that the error of that coordinate is exaggerated or divided by zero. The norm of Hairer, Norsett and Wanner uses max(|q_second|, |q_start|), as the Python step size controller of exudyn.symbolics.advancedSolvers. Decided: fixed with the common step size controller in C++ (revision2026c step RG20.8).
releaseNotes: ODE23 and DOPRI5 scale the error of each coordinate by absoluteTolerance + relativeTolerance*max(|q_new|, |q_start|), with the absolute values, and take their step sizes from the PI controller shared with the implicit Runge-Kutta solvers instead of the elementary rule; the steps and results of these solvers change slightly, the errors of the test models became smaller; explicitStepSizeControlTest.py.
